summary: Grading is a pure function of the four submitted plan files, verifier-owned hash-checked day copies, a fixed targets file and exact integer arithmetic; no randomness, clock, network, ordering or timing dependency reaches the graded result.

files_read: environment/app/days/day-1.json (lines 1-40 and 1275-1314 read; all four day files scanned by pattern for top-level keys and for any decimal or exponent number)
unread_or_truncated_ranges: tests/days/day-{1..4}.json.gz are binary gzip and were not decompressed; their content is pinned at grading time by the SHA-256 and count check in tests/test_outputs.py:30-40 against tests/days/roster.json, whose hashes equal the manifest hashes of environment/app/days/day-{1..4}.json, so the graded data is fixed regardless.

Bulk numeric bodies of environment/app/days/day-*.json and solution/plans/day-{2,3,4}.json and the remainder of solution/plans/day-1.json were not read line by line; they are fixed data files whose values cannot vary between runs, and a pattern scan confirmed the day files contain no non-integer numbers.

checks_performed: Traced tests/test.sh: fixed pytest invocation with -p no:randomly and -p no:cacheprovider in a fresh mktemp dir; reward derived only from pytest exit code (tests/test.sh:13-21).

Traced tests/test_outputs.py: targets and roster loaded from verifier-owned files; each day read from verifier gzip copy and checked by SHA-256 and counts; plan loaded with load_plan and scored with verifier's own evaluate (tests/test_outputs.py:21-55).

Traced tests/check_plan.py evaluate: only dict/list iteration over fixed data and the plan in its file order; overlap check sorts by (arrive, depart, tid); cost is integer sum; no randomness, time or environment reads (tests/check_plan.py:76-131).

Confirmed all numbers in the four day files are integers (no decimal point or exponent matches), so cost is exact integer arithmetic and the <= target comparison cannot flicker on float summation order.

Confirmed roster sha256 values equal the manifest hashes of environment/app/days/day-{1..4}.json and tests/targets.json equals environment/app/days/targets.json by hash (packet-manifest.json:12-16,29-35; tests/days/roster.json:6,12,18,24).

Checked dependencies: both images pin the python:3.13-slim-bookworm base by digest; pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2 pinned; verifier runs with network no-network; no remote data is read at grading (environment/Dockerfile:1, tests/Dockerfile:1-3, task.toml:18-21).

Checked solution: solve.sh only copies fixed saved plans and checks them with the checker; search.py's seeded RNG and wall-clock budget are not run by the oracle (solution/solve.sh:24-36, solution/search.py:196-239).
Checked timing: verifier work is linear in turns/transfers plus small pairwise wingtip checks, far within verifier timeout_sec=1800; no sleeps or readiness waits exist.

coverage_sweep.category: Fresh random seeds / generated corpora; boundary cases as guaranteed fixtures
coverage_sweep.reason: Verifier uses four fixed day files hash-checked against a roster; no generator or RNG exists in tests. The only RNG is solution/search.py's explicit seeded random.Random(seed), which the oracle does not execute.

coverage_sweep.category: Current date or time / evaluation clock
coverage_sweep.reason: Times in the rules are fixed minute integers from the day files; no verifier code reads the clock. time.time() appears only in the unexecuted search script's run budget.

Base images pinned by digest; pytest and ctrf plugin pinned; verifier and agent run with no network; days, targets and checker are local verifier copies. Unpinned transitive pytest deps and unpinned apt tools (tmux, asciinema) are image-build inputs that do not affect how evaluate scores a plan.

coverage_sweep.category: Filesystem or iteration ordering; sorted where order is required, equivalent orderings accepted otherwise
coverage_sweep.reason: The contract allows turn ids in any order and stands omitted or empty; evaluate's validity and cost are order-independent (buffer check sorts occupancy, cost is a commutative integer sum, dict order follows file order which is fixed for a given submission). No directory listing is used by the verifier; plan paths are named explicitly.

coverage_sweep.category: Numeric stability of the graded comparison
coverage_sweep.reason: All day-file numbers are integers and plan values used in cost are only string ids, so cost is exact and cost <= target is stable. Reference plans sit exactly on targets, which is safe under exact integer arithmetic.
No services, sleeps or waits in the verifier; scoring is a bounded in-process computation; plan size capped at 2,000,000 bytes and nesting at 64 so parse time is bounded.
Each test recomputes from files with no mutation of module state; pytest-randomly disabled and cache provider off, so order or cache cannot change outcome.

coverage_sweep.category: Repeated clean-run stability for correct and incorrect submissions
coverage_sweep.reason: Statically, a fixed plan maps to a fixed PlanError/cost and fixed pass/fail on every run; the oracle's fixed plans yield cost equal to target each run. Not executed; static trace only.

rules: plan lists in any order (stand-rules.md file format)
buffer rule check on a stand
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Same stand assignment written with turn ids in different list orders: evaluate sorts occupancy by (arrive, depart, tid) before pairwise buffer checks, so validity is identical.
Wingtip stand omitted from plan: plan['stands'].get(a, []) yields empty list deterministically, independent of dict order.
Candidate edits /app/days or /app/tools during the agent phase: verifier uses its own gzip days hash-checked against roster and its own check_plan.py, so grading input is fixed across runs.
Plan whose cost equals the target exactly (the reference): integer arithmetic makes the <= comparison exact, no float-order drift.
